ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 and L.561-2-3 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier); Implementing Decree No. 2017-1094 of 2 August 2017 on the register of beneficial owners (RBE); Article L.123-10 and R.123-165 of the French Commercial Code; Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, Registered Agent)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate service provider or board of directors of the shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for incorporation and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil/police authority or attested by a notary of the UBO's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory self-declaration and automated screening of all UBOs, directors and signatories against EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UNSC Consolidated List, French national freezes (Tracfin), and OFAC SDN/51% rule where applicable under French banking practice; enhanced due diligence for PEPs under CMF Art. L.561-10 and EU Directive 2015/849 as amended; 24-hour re-screening and negative media monitoring; any nexus to a non-cooperative high-risk jurisdiction triggers additional SoF/SoW verification.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); RCS records consulted via Infogreffe (infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be registered in Latin characters; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated. The Toubon Law (Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994) imposes French for statutory labelling and consumer-facing contracts; the proposed name must be distinctive, lawful, non-misleading and not contrary to public order.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No separate reservation or extension exists in France; name protection is effective on RCS registration. If the Guichet Unique rejects the name, the applicant must re-file a corrected dossier. A formal refusal by the Greffier may be challenged within 15 days via a request to the President of the Tribunal de commerce (requête en autorisation d'immatriculation) under Article R.123-20 of the Commercial Code; a prior-right objection may be cured by consent, surrender, or selection of a new name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only through a licensed domiciliation provider (domiciliataire) under Commercial Code Art. L.123-10 and R.123-165; the provider must maintain a physical address in France and forward mail. For an ISIC 4669 wholesale commodity trader, a virtual office is accepted as a correspondence address but does not by itself satisfy the substance requirement for French tax residence or for a bank relationship; accounting records must be kept at a determinable address within France.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 15% annual probability of an unannounced tax or URSSAF inspection in the first three years; customs/phytosanitary physical checks are inventory-based and do not generally target the registered office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title II, Chapter VII, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-2 and L.227-9; Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 on formation; Decree No. 2021-300 on the single business registration portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (local commercial court registry), with electronic intake through the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) Guichet unique at www.formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration unique d'immatriculation (single registration application) together with the statuts (articles of association), filed pursuant to Articles R.123-1 et seq. of the Commercial Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for an SAS. The capital is freely fixed in the statuts; in-kind contributions must be fully released at subscription, while cash contributions must be paid in at least 50% at subscription and the balance within five years. No mandatory state escrow account applies, but cash funds must be deposited in a bank blocked until registration unless the statutes provide otherwise.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The share subscription table is approved; the capital of €[●], divided into [●] ordinary shares, is subscribed in full, each subscriber paying all in-kind contributions and at least 50% of cash contributions. (2) The proposed articles are adopted, and the registered office is fixed at [●], where books and minutes will be kept. (3) The registered office address is accepted for statutory seat purposes. (4) [●] is appointed President for an indefinite time, with full and unrestricted day-to-day management power toward third parties, within the provisions of Articles L.227-1 and L.227-9. (5) The President is authorized to execute the incorporation filings, publish announcements, appoint representatives, and take all steps to register the company. This resolution becomes effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, sign and fund the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders' meeting; a French notary is required only where a real-property contribution is made.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare French-language statuts setting out the SAS governance structure, share capital, share classes, presidency, and registered-office clause. Allocate shares and execute the subscription schedule. Deposit cash contributions into a French bank account and obtain a blocking certificate; for in-kind contributions, obtain a statutory auditor's report on the valuation. Sign the statuts by all shareholders in private writing or before a notary where applicable.
required_dossiers: Attestation de dépôt des fonds (bank certificate of blocked capital)
Rapport du commissaire aux apports where in-kind contributions are made
Valid identity documents of each subscriber and the proposed President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a document is incomplete or legally inconsistent, the founders sign a corrective deed and amend the bank certificate or auditor's report before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the single registration application on the Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Guichet unique portal and create an application for the registration of a commercial legal entity (SAS). Select the appropriate RCS registration category, upload the signed statuts, publication proof, bank certificate, president's office acceptance and declarations, beneficial-ownership declaration (RBE), and registered-office occupation documents. Elect to publish the legal notice via the portal if required. Submit the dossier and pay the registry fees, then retain the electronic acknowledgement of receipt.
required_dossiers: Receipt of publication of the notice of incorporation in an approved legal advertisement gazette
Letter of acceptance of the President's office and declaration of no criminal conviction
Proof of registered-office address (lease, free occupation declaration, or domiciliation contract)
Identity documents of shareholders and President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the corrective response must be submitted through the same portal within the prescribed delay; if the registry formally refuses, the decision may be contested before the President of the commercial court after an amicable rectification attempt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Kbis extract and post-registration identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation by the commercial court registry, the SAS is entered in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS). Verify the issued Kbis extract, the SIREN and SIRET numbers, the APE classification code, and the French VAT identification number. Retain the registration order as proof that the company has legal personality.
required_dossiers: No additional dossier; the official Kbis extract is issued by the registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is delayed or contains inaccurate data, request a priority rectification from the greffe; any error in statutory entries is corrected through a separate registration amendment application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure commercial wholesaling of prilled urea and potassium chloride; no industrial licensing body is triggered. If the entity later installs large-scale physical storage subject to ICPE thresholds, the competent authority is the Préfet of the department, supported by the DREAL.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required — no operating permit or manufacturing license is necessary for an unregulated wholesaling activity under French commercial law; RCS registration is the sole statutory status.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Non-applicable; should a future fixed installation be created, the competent authority would be Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) under the Ministry of Ecological Transition.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the proposed administrative and commercial wholesale activity does not fall within the EIA listing or an ICPE authorization/registration category; no impact study is required at formation stage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No specific discharge thresholds are triggered by the pure wholesale activity. If incidental warehousing of solid mineral fertilizers is introduced, operators must ensure dust suppression, prevention of fugitive emissions, and conformity with municipal wastewater discharge standards and the general occupational hygiene requirements of the Code du travail.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire-safety operating license is required for ordinary office or warehouse space; however, if the premises are open to a workforce, the employer must prepare the unique risk-assessment document (DUERP), verify electrical and fire-safety conformity under the Code du travail, and, for relevant racking or mezzanine structures, secure structural load inspection by a qualified controller. Where the premises constitute an ERP (établissement recevant du public), a fire-safety commission visit may apply.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), operating under the French Ministry of Economy and Finance; public portal at www.impots.gouv.fr; corporate formalities portal at www.formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned SAS or a French branch of a non-resident entity must first register the legal entity or branch with the French Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through the online formalities portal, obtaining a SIREN and SIRET number. Thereafter, the DGFiP automatically or on application issues a French VAT number in the format 'FR + 2-digit key + 9-digit SIREN'. Non-EU entities without a permanent establishment in France that carry out taxable supplies in France must appoint an accredited fiscal representative (représentant fiscal accrédité) for VAT and obtain the VAT ID through that representative. Application is made to the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No discretionary check-the-box election is available for an SAS; it is mandatorily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at entity level. Available statutory mechanisms include: election for consolidated French tax group filing (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI for entities at least 95% controlled by a French head company; election to form a single-tax VAT group (assujetti unique) under Article 256 C bis CGI; and application of the EU ATAD hybrid mismatch rules with possible offsetting adjustment elections where recognised by the French tax authorities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For non-established foreign suppliers, there is no registration threshold: any taxable supply made in France triggers a VAT registration obligation. For established French domestic businesses, the small-business exemption threshold is EUR 85,000 of annual turnover for supplies of goods (and EUR 183,300 for certain supplies of services), but this relief is not available to foreign persons without a fixed establishment in France.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has a phased mandatory B2B e-invoicing and e-reporting regime. From 1 September 2026, all large enterprises must issue structured electronic invoices (Factur-X, UBL or CII) through Chorus Pro or a certified private dematerialisation platform (PDP); from 1 September 2027, all VAT-registered businesses must comply. Invoice transaction data and payment status data must be transmitted to DGFiP in near real time for fiscal clearance and pre-filling of VAT returns. Physical stamping is not used, but digital fiscal data transmission is mandatory; operators not using a certified PDP must connect directly to Chorus Pro.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union may be zero-rated for VAT under Article 262-I of the French General Tax Code (CGI), provided the supplier holds evidence that the goods left the EU territory. Offshore supplies of services to non-resident counterparties may be zero-rated or outside scope under Articles 259 and 259 B CGI where the place of supply rules apply. Fertilizer and potash sales to non-EU buyers qualify for 0% VAT if the export evidence and commercial documentation are complete and consistent.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (déclaration en douane - DAU)
Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document (B/L, CMR, AWB)
Dual-use / restricted goods declarations if applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The French tax administration may refuse the export VAT exemption and reassess VAT at 20% where the exporter fails to produce the required export proof or where documents are false or knowingly irregular. Deliberate tax fraud (manquement délibéré) triggers an 80% administrative penalty under Article 1731 CGI plus late-payment interest (intérêt de retard), and in criminal cases fines and imprisonment under the tax fraud provisions may apply. Any VAT recovered or deducted on export transactions may be clawed back retrospectively with penalties where the export zero-rating conditions are found not to have been satisfied.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) as the French central bank and monetary authority; ACPR (Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution) as the banking, e-money and payment-institution licensing and AML/CFT supervisory authority; Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) at the Ministry of Economy and Finance for foreign investment review (IEF) and external financial relations. The applicable legal framework is the Code monétaire et financier (CMF). Article L.521-1 CMF enshrines the principle that financial relations between France and foreign countries are free, subject to the safeguards in Articles L.511-1 et seq. and L.561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account. France maintains no distinction between current and capital account for exchange-control purposes, and there is no prior exchange authorization for cross-border payments by an SAS resident in France. Profit and dividend remittance is unrestricted: an SAS may distribute dividends in EUR or in an agreed foreign currency via SWIFT/SEPA after a shareholders' resolution; the distribution is subject to the standard French withholding tax (generally 25% for non-resident corporate shareholders, or treaty-reduced rates). Cross-border financial flows are monitored for statistical purposes: the servicing French bank reports all flows to the Banque de France under the balance-of-payments framework (EU Regulation 184/2014 and the national nomenclature of international transactions), assigning the applicable purpose code; no prior approval is required. The key convertibility-linked constraints for a physical urea and potash wholesale charter vehicle are not FX restrictions but EU trade measures: (i) under Council Regulation (EU) 833/2014 as amended by the 16th sanctions package (Council Regulation (EU) 2025/395 of 24 February 2025), the purchase and import of potash (CN 3104/3105) originating in Russia or exported from Russia is restricted to an annual quota until 10 July 2026, with a full import prohibition thereafter; (ii) imports of certain nitrogenous fertilizers (e.g., urea ammonium nitrate solutions, solid urea) from Russia may be subject to definitive EU anti-dumping or countervailing duties; (iii) payments relating to sanctioned persons, vessels, or charter parties are prohibited unless covered by a license. These items are managed through customs and compliance screening rather than through FX controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no holding period for export receipts. An EU-resident exporter may retain EUR or foreign-currency balances in any bank account in France or abroad, may entertain netting arrangements, and may freely use forwards or other hedging instruments. The only applicable obligations are (i) the standard monthly balance-of-payments statistical declaration submitted by the intermediary bank to the Banque de France, and (ii) sanctions and anti-dumping verification for cargoes originating in or transiting territories subject to EU restrictive measures (in particular Russian/Belarusian potash and urea).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte de dépôt de fonds pour constitution) and Operational EUR/USD Accounts with commodity trade finance desk
Capital Escrow Account and Operational EUR/USD Accounts with documentary credit (MT700) and FBF FX line capabilities

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole CIB / LCL (Crédit Agricole regional banks)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and trade finance facilities (LC confirmation, pre-export finance); escrow opened only upon acceptance of the full commercial relationship
Operational Account with structured commodity trade finance desk (LCs, guarantees, supply-chain finance)
Operational Account and documentary credit services; escrow possible on a case-by-case basis

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility for operational EUR/USD settlement (SEPA, SWIFT MT103 outbound, multi-currency wallet) through ACPR-licensed French electronic money institutions (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Mangopay) or through EU-passported EMIs under PSD2 (e.g., Wise Europe, Airwallex EU). Legal constraints: (i) a non-EEA EMI cannot lawfully provide payment accounts in France unless it establishes a French-licensed entity or operates through a ACPR-approved e-money agent; (ii) an EU EMI passporting into France must complete the ACPR notification procedure; (iii) EMIs are not credit institutions and are not permitted to issue or confirm documentary credits (MT7xx), grant commodity trade finance, or provide FX forwards or swaps, which limits the utility of this route for ISIC 4669 physical commodity clearing. Rating: Medium for operational collection and disbursement; Low for LC-based trade flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French tier-1 banks generally require the statutory representative (Président) of the SAS and any non-resident UBO or authorized signatory to attend at least one physical in-branch interview, or a certified remote video onboarding with a high-grade notarized signature (signature électronique avancée) and apostilled corporate documents. A fully remote opening is typically accepted only where the client already holds an active relationship with the bank or where a French-registered domiciliation agent, notary, or accountant physically certifies the identity of the signatories. A non-resident UBO owning the SAS triggers enhanced due diligence and, in practice, a 4-10 week onboarding including: notarized/legalized powers of attorney, certified passport copies, proof of address, 3-month personal and entity bank statements, source-of-wealth statement, and a video interview with the AML/KYC committee. The digital-first banks (Qonto, Shine) permit fully remote opening, but they cannot deliver LC issuance or trade finance capacity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO with no French or EEA tax residence controlling a newly registered French SAS (typical third-country direct-investment vehicle)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis excerpt (issued within 3 months); signed Statuts; UBO declaration filed at the Greffe (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); passport and proof of address of the UBO; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statement; parent-company audited financial statements (or 6 months bank statements if unaudited); group organizational chart; detailed business plan describing the fertilizer wholesale and charter activity; list of first eight target customers and suppliers; signed AML questionnaire of the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commodity flows involving Russia, Belarus, or sanctioned ports (potash, urea, NPK) — elevated sanctions and PEP/reputational risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening output on all counterparties, beneficial owners, vessel owners, and charterers; certificates of origin (non-Russian or non-Belarusian origin); Bill of Lading and cargo survey reports (SGS, Intertek); full AIS voyage history of the vessel; where the cargo is Russian potash within the authorized quota, the relevant quota certificate and DGDDI customs entry; written compliance policy confirming EU/OFAC/UN sanctions screening at 100% of transactions; contractual warranties from the supplier excluding sanctioned supply chains; evidence that the French importer is registered with the relevant customs and fertilizer product regulations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Physical chartering business with no material substance (no operational office, no staff, no warehouse) in France — trade-based money laundering risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master charter party and voyage charter contracts; commodity sale and purchase agreements; pro-forma and final commercial invoices; independent commodity inspection certificates (SGS, Intertek, Alex Stewart); cash-flow and working-capital forecast; storage and handling agreements at French ports; statutory accounts of the SAS after first closing; confirmation that the company is the contractual charterer and principal, not a pass-through intermediary; copies of bank trade lines and LC documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Settlement to third parties or to accounts in jurisdictions with no nexus to the underlying cargo
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully reconciled invoices matched to LC terms; approved payee list signed by two authorized signatories; treasury policy on dual-control payments; explanation of the commercial reason for each destination country; documentary evidence of physical cargo movement (warehouse receipts, port discharge reports, weight certificates, mate's receipts); any intermediary mandates or sub-charter agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency USD/EUR conversion without a documented hedging policy — bank risk committee may classify the SAS as a quasi-financial entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy approved by the SAS board including FX exposure limits, hedging horizon, and permissible instruments; FBF Master Agreement (Contrat-Cadre) signature sheet; mandate for forward foreign exchange transactions; description of the natural hedge between USD-linked purchase prices and EUR-linked sales; evidence of the capital injection and shareholder loan structure confirming medium-term solvency; line-item confirmation that the SAS does not carry speculative open FX positions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a capital contribution, share premium, or shareholder loan from a non-resident parent into the French SAS: (i) from the EEA, use a SEPA Credit Transfer; from outside the EEA, use SWIFT MT103; (ii) instruct the remitting bank to identify the transfer as a capital operation in the Remittance Information field (e.g., 'Capital increase - SAS [name]' or 'Shareholder loan agreement dated [date]') and to apply the standard Banque de France balance-of-payments category for direct investment creation/capital increase; for a loan, the intercompany loan category applies; (iii) the French receiving bank requires the corporate supporting file (Kbis, signed shareholders' resolution or president's decision, notarized or witnessed certificate of deposit for capital, copy of the loan agreement for shareholder debt) and screens the funds under the ACPR AML framework; (iv) no exchange authorization is required under Article L.521-1 CMF. Where the contribution exceeds EUR 1,000,000, the bank will conduct enhanced source-of-funds verification (audited accounts of the transferor, chain-of-funds statements), and the receipt must be reported in the monthly BOP statement. Capital increases must be reflected at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within one month; the escrow account release is executed upon presentation of the certificate of registration (certificat d'immatriculation/kbis).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for physical urea and potash charter transactions: (i) SWIFT MT103 for open-account settlement of supplier invoices, charter hire, port costs, and surveyor fees, with complete narrative (contract reference, invoice number, Incoterms, BOP purpose code) and sanctions screening on beneficiary, intermediary banks, and underlying vessel; (ii) SWIFT MT700 for issuance/amendment of irrevocable documentary credits under UCP600, where the French bank is the issuing bank and the beneficiary is the fertilizer producer or trading house; the LC proceeds settle via TARGET2 for EUR or via Fedwire/CHIPS correspondent rails for USD; (iii) SWIFT MT760 for standby LCs guaranteeing charterer performance or demurrage obligations; (iv) SWIFT MT202/MT202 COV for bank-to-bank cover payments in correspondent banking. For EUR-denominated LC settlement, TARGET2 provides same-day finality; for USD settlement, the clearing path is the correspondent account at the New York Fed/bank. The French exporting entity may also request the beneficiary to provide certificates of origin, phytosanitary documents (where required), and vessel pre-arrival notices to release the LC documents.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forwards (forward foreign exchange contracts) in EUR/USD and EUR/GBP, executed under the FBF 2018 Master Agreement (Contrat-Cadre relatif aux opérations de change) with the account bank; these are the standard hedging instruments for the expected USD-billed cargo periods.
FX swaps (change à terme / swap de change) EUR/USD to convert temporary foreign currency liquidity and match the timing of charter payments versus sales proceeds.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) for longer-dated hedging of committed cargo purchase programs, subject to an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the FBF swap annex, with appropriate EMIR documentation for a non-financial counterparty (NFC) below the clearing threshold.

OTC EUR/USD FX options (European call/put and zero-cost collars) for asymmetric risk protection, permissible for French non-financial corporates as treasury instruments and settled through the FBF or ISDA framework.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted third-country currencies (e.g., COP, EGP, PKR, NGN) where the cargo is sourced from a producer country whose currency is not freely deliverable; settlement is in USD or EUR under an ISDA-based confirmation, with the French bank acting as pricing counterparty and permissibly structured under EU EMIR rules.

Cross-commodity and freight-linked derivatives (FFA - Forward Freight Agreements) commonly used alongside the FX book to fix the charter legs in USD; these are permissible as commodity derivatives under EMIR for the SAS in its capacity as physical charterer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual financial statements (bilan and compte de résultat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS France)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 6 months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to €1,500 per month of delay; risk of company administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Exceeding two of the following thresholds: turnover > €50 million, balance sheet total > €43 million, or number of employees > 500
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (PCG) or IFRS if applicable

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual internal review and update of the beneficial ownership register; mandatory update upon any change in shareholding or control

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2022
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of annual taxable profit for qualifying SMEs, generally with turnover below EUR 10 million and at least 75% of share capital held by individuals or small companies; Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million; Innovation Tax Credit for SMEs at 20%; preferential 10% rate for qualifying patent box income
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward with no statutory expiration, subject to an annual offset cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million; loss carryback available for the preceding year up to EUR 1 million

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (déclaration de résultats) with schedules 2050-SD to 2059-SD, filed electronically through the DGFiP professional portal (impots.gouv.fr) using EFI or EDI mode; required for all SAS entities irrespective of non-resident shareholding
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing; quarterly CIT instalments generally due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with the balancing payment due at the annual filing deadline
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a 31 December fiscal year-end, the electronic return is due by 3 May of the following year (deferred to the next business day if 3 May is not a business day); for non-calendar fiscal year-ends, the return is due within three months of the balance sheet date, subject to the statutory extension to the second business day following 1 May for calendar-year taxpayers

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter SIREN, SIRET, APE/NAF code 4669Z, legal form SAS, registered office, tax reference and electronic filing channel code
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SAS is the resident taxpayer; non-resident directors and shareholders are not entitled to file on behalf of the entity without a formal power of attorney, and the entity must use a French tax representative if electronic filing infrastructure is hosted abroad

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare gross revenue excluding VAT from wholesale trading of prilled urea, potassium chloride and related fertilizer commodities, including export sales invoiced from France
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All turnover generated through the French SAS is reportable in France; ownership by non-residents does not change the French source characterization of the sales

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Net Accounting Income Before Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the accounting net profit before tax under French GAAP after charging cost of goods sold, freight, logistics, insurance, bank charges and selling expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SAS must apply full accrual accounting; no reduction is permitted for profits expected to be remitted to non-resident shareholders

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back non-deductible expenses, excessive director compensation, non-deductible fines, disallowed interest under thin-capitalization rules and non-arm's length related-party charges; deduct qualifying exempt long-term capital gains and eligible participation exemptions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party expenses paid to non-resident suppliers must be supported by contracts, arm's length benchmarks and evidence of actual services or goods; otherwise they are reclassified as constructive dividends subject to withholding tax

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Taxable Income and Tax Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income after loss carryforwards, apply the 15% reduced-rate tranche where eligible, apply the 25% standard rate and deduct available tax credits such as CIR
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Entity-level CIT is assessed on the French SAS in full; no deduction or deferral is available merely because the ultimate beneficiary is non-resident

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a statutory 10% increase of the assessed corporate tax under CGI Article 1728, increased to 40% where the omission is intentional and 80% where fraudulent; monthly late-payment interest of 0.20% applies; failure to file within 30 days after formal notice may trigger ex officio assessment, reversal of burden of proof and additional fines

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under CGI Article 119 bis for dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders; 30% flat levy applies to non-resident individual shareholders (12.8% income tax plus 17.2% social levies); reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the EU parent holds at least 5% for 24 months; DTA rates generally range from 0% to 15%
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The reduced treaty rate is not automatic: the non-resident beneficial owner must provide a tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the competent foreign authority to the French paying company before payment, file Cerfa Form 5000 for general treaty relief or Form 5001 for EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, and satisfy the treaty's beneficial ownership and anti-abuse conditions; if the excess withholding has already been borne, the beneficiary may apply for a refund under the French tax refund procedure
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: arm's length interest paid by a French company to a non-resident lender is generally exempt from French withholding tax, reduced to 0% under most tax treaties and under the EU Interest-Royalty Directive for associated EU companies; however, payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions are taxed at 75%. Royalties: domestic withholding tax of 33.33% applies to payments for patents and industrial property rights under CGI Article 182 B; reduced to 0% under the EU Interest-Royalty Directive for qualifying EU associated companies and under many DTAs, while non-treaty royalties remain subject to the domestic rate

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: In EUR: full Master File and Local File obligations arise where the French entity's annual turnover or gross assets exceed EUR 400 million; Country-by-Country Reporting arises where the ultimate parent's consolidated group revenue equals or exceeds EUR 750 million; even below these thresholds, the French tax administration may require transfer pricing information under Article L.13 B of the French Tax Procedures Code upon audit request
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP - Comparable Uncontrolled Price, particularly for quoted urea and potash commodity benchmarks
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply a standalone Economic Substance Regulation, but the EU ATAD General Anti-Abuse Rule, French abuse-of-law doctrine (Article L.64 of the Tax Procedures Code), and the OECD Multilateral Instrument Principal Purpose Test require genuine commercial substance, local decision-making, personnel, physical activity and real risk absorption; an invoicing-only fertilizer conduit with no trading substance can be recharacterized and denied treaty benefits

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting fertilizer commodity sales, maintaining unreported offshore bank accounts, creating fictitious purchase invoices from shell suppliers, or destroying shipping and documentary credit records to understate French taxable profit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative reassessment with 40% bad-faith penalty or 80% fraudulent-maneuver penalty; criminal conviction under CGI Article 1741 carries up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 75,000 fine, increased to seven years and EUR 250,000 when committed by an organized group; confiscation of proceeds and publication orders may also be imposed
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be criminally prosecuted personally, ordered to pay civil restitution, subjected to asset freezes and travel bans, disqualified from management, and held jointly liable for corporate tax debts under Article L.267 of the Tax Procedures Code where their serious fault caused non-collection of tax

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Abusive Conduit Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing the French SAS as a letterbox entity without staff, premises, inventory, trading authority or risk control, while routing urea and potash wholesale margin to related non-resident companies through artificial service fees or inflated cost of goods
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the whole arrangement under Article L.64 of the Tax Procedures Code with an 80% abuse-of-law penalty; possible denial of treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test; additional 100% penalty where the abuse is proven to be adopted with fraudulent intent
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil piercing on grounds of fictitious company or alter ego; directors face personal civil liability for restitution, criminal fines, travel bans, professional disqualification and, in insolvency, activation of commercial liability for fraudulent mismanagement

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying non-arm's length margins on intra-group fertilizer trades, failing to prepare or produce Master File and Local File, refusing to respond to the tax authority's transfer pricing information request within 30 days, or using excessive related-party interest to strip taxable profit from France
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm's length reallocation of profit, reassessment of CIT and withholding taxes, late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, and administrative penalties for failure to present transfer pricing documentation, potentially reaching 5% of reassessed amounts or additional flat fines; deliberate non-compliance attracts the 80% penalty
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved artificial intra-group pricing may be held personally liable for the resulting tax loss, subjected to fines, ordered to compensate the company, and prosecuted under abuse-of-law rules where the arrangement concealed fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using third-party front companies for Swift LC or wire transfer settlements, structuring payments to avoid reporting thresholds, concealing ultimate beneficial ownership of the SAS, or processing commodity payments through shell banks with no underlying physical movement of urea or potash
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering under French Penal Code Articles 324-1 and 324-2 carries up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine for individuals; aggravated money laundering carries up to ten years and EUR 750,000; legal entities face multiplied fines, dissolution and confiscation orders; false currency declarations trigger separate customs monetary penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal conviction, confiscation of illicit assets, travel bans, withdrawal of passport, disqualification from company management and personal civil liability in subsequent insolvency or shareholder proceedings
